[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] The Pittock Block is a mixed-use building in downtown Portland, Oregon, built in 1913 by publisher Henry Pittock, designed by Doyle, Patterson & Beach with reinforced concrete construction, listed on the National Register of Historic Places since 1987 and recognized as a Portland Historic Landmark. Per the source consulted this session, the building today serves as a significant data infrastructure location, housing a NWAX Point of Presence, described as Portlands internet exchange point, alongside other tenants including the City Club of Portland and administrative offices for the Oregon Symphony.

While this confirms the buildings role as a telecommunications interconnection point, the source consulted this session did not name a specific commercial building owner or data-center operator company responsible for the facility, unlike comparable carrier-hotel buildings elsewhere in this registry such as 32 Avenue of the Americas or the Terminal Commerce Building, where a named real estate owner could be identified. No operator attribution is made for this facility and none is fabricated; this remains an open research item pending identification of the buildings current ownership or a named facility operator.
